reporter_ref: PR #4701 pre-merge adversarial review (Codex+Kimi panel, adjudicated by FortitudeEtc)
trigger: a rogue ProxyRegister/register_fresh against an already-affinity-bound agent never confirms via announce_connected, then waits kTombstonePurgeAgeSecs (300s) for reap_stale_routes()'s tombstone-purge sweep to run
summary: Empirically reproduced against real Postgres (rogue register_fresh -> sweep -> rogue TOFU-rebind, home_cluster_id ends at the rogue's cluster): sweep (b)'s hard-delete predicate (lease_until IS NULL AND updated_at < cutoff) had no regard for a bound home_cluster_id, so a single rogue claim-and-wait fully purged the row (wiping the sticky affinity along with it) and reopened a TOFU rebind window ADR-2002 SS7d's own "requires the real cluster to have been genuinely unreachable" guarantee explicitly promised could not happen. FIXED: sweep (b) now excludes any row with a bound home_cluster_id unconditionally; a new sweep (b') soft-tombstones (session/cluster/node/home cleared, home_cluster_id PRESERVED) a session-bearing row that would otherwise have matched, so a rogue's abandoned claim can never force a re-home. New tests: the rogue-register-then-wait falsifier (proves tombstones_reaped==0, affinity_preserved_soft_tombstones==1, home_cluster_id survives, rogue still refused afterward, real cluster can still reconnect) and the ordinary-deregister-with-affinity parked-forever case.

line: 'reap_stale_routes purges a tombstone past the purge age' and the PR #4299 EvalPlanQual BLOCKER-2 concurrency test
summary: The tombstone-purge test's fixture row now matched the NEW sweep (b') predicate's exclusion (home_cluster_id bound), so it silently stopped being purged -- a genuine test regression, not caught until the broader suite was run against real Postgres (the earlier [affinity]-tag-only run did not include either test). The EvalPlanQual test's row no longer became a sweep-(b) candidate at all, so the concurrency race it exists to force never happened -- REQUIRE(blocked) failed false, and because that REQUIRE ran before reaper.join(), the still-joinable std::thread's destructor called std::terminate() (SIGABRT) instead of reporting a clean test failure. FIXED: both tests' fixture rows no longer call announce_connected (staying genuine no-affinity tombstones, preserving each test's original intent); the EvalPlanQual test's commit+join sequence was also reordered to run unconditionally before any REQUIRE that could throw, closing the thread-leak/terminate hazard for good regardless of future assertion outcomes.

reporter_ref: PR #4701 pre-merge adversarial re-review round 2 (Codex+Kimi panel, adjudicated by FortitudeEtc), empirically reproduced independently by both
trigger: round 1's soft-tombstone sweep (b') clears a session-bearing affinity-bound row's durable session_id (while preserving home_cluster_id) after kTombstonePurgeAgeSecs; the ORIGINAL rogue's session stays live in the gateway's in-memory gateway_sessions_ (a refused CONNECTED never invalidates it, and the Erlang gateway ignores acknowledged=false), so the rogue resends CONNECTED under that same still-live session once the row is orphaned
summary: Both affinity-classification probes matched only session_id=$2 exactly, which a durable NULL (the session-orphaned row left by round 1's own soft-tombstone) can never satisfy, so the rogue's resend fell through to the ordinary, unaudited session_mismatch bucket instead of cluster_affinity_violation -- no rollback (unpublish_gateway_route is only called from the violation branch), no alert. The durable row itself was never fooled (home_cluster_id stays correct throughout, confirmed by the reporter's own repro), but the in-memory dispatch route (AgentSession::cluster_id, what send_to/send_to_all actually read) silently took the rogue's cluster -- falsifying ADR-2002 SS7d's own claim that a rogue's subsequent CONNECTED can no longer move the dispatch target to its cluster. FIXED: both probes' WHERE clauses extended from session_id=$2 to (session_id=$2 OR session_id IS NULL), so a session-orphaned row with a bound, differing home_cluster_id is now caught -- refused before publish for the common case (the pre-check itself), with announce_connected's own probe and unpublish_gateway_route remaining defense-in-depth. A genuine first-ever TOFU contact is unaffected: that row always has home_cluster_id IS NULL, already excluded by the predicate's own IS NOT NULL clause regardless of session_id. New wiring-level regression test (real GatewayUpstreamServiceImpl + real Postgres) reproduces the full attack sequence end-to-end and proves the resend is now refused, the in-memory route is never published, and the durable affinity survives.
